note: Deleting or reindexing the single event A_0 transfers the stated n>=1 frequency law immediately; the corollary's claim and unbounded-count argument are correct, and only that finite-prefix sentence is omitted.

The closing assertion is false at an interval endpoint under the published relative-domain derivative convention: the derivative may exist while the two unavailable-side Dini derivatives are undefined.
For a=b the displayed right limit defining beta_a is not well posed, so the purported jump function is undefined on an allowed compact interval.

The published interval definition includes unbounded closed intervals, but the fine-cover predicate applies an undefined length to every member; the family must be restricted to bounded closed nondegenerate intervals.

The statement is unconditional but the term-by-term theorem used to prove the constructed function singular explicitly assumes Countable Choice. The same proof also needs the published Cantor continuity and Cantor-null interfaces.
The Example calls the Cantor function increasing, which means strictly increasing in the library; the cited interface says it is nondecreasing and constant on removed intervals.

Under the library's at-most-countable enumeration convention repetitions are allowed, in which case a repeated rational's jump is the sum of all corresponding weights rather than 2^{-n}; the witness must require no repetitions.

The derivative-zero conclusion invokes a theorem whose statement assumes Countable Choice, but the example never assumes that axiom; listing its definition as a dependency does not supply the hypothesis.
The title says all four values are distinct, while the correctly computed values are 1, -1, 1, -1; only two distinct values occur.

The dependency's statement is exactly the displayed zero-one conclusion, and its proof establishes tail membership. The Example only overcompresses that proof into L1; step 1.1 is an immediate direct instantiation.
Step 1.1 makes the false strict claim that the Cantor function is increasing. Nondecreasing is the property that makes the variation sum telescope and is what the cited theorem supplies.

The immediately available published corollary proves continuity of the Cantor function from the cited Cantor properties. Adding that direct citation closes the local bridge; the constructed witness and refutation are otherwise correct.
The unrestricted exactly-when claim is false for the library's domain-relative derivative at interval endpoints; four-way agreement is equivalent only at an interior point of the interval.

The midpoint claim for Poisson means follows immediately by combining the preceding Fejer midpoint theorem with Cesaro-implies-Abel. The remark omits those direct links, but the qualitative comparison is true.

Negating the reflected function makes it nondecreasing and interchanges the relevant left/right Dini derivatives. This is an immediate sign correction to step 3.1; the null-set argument and theorem remain correct.
Replacing m(y)=prod y_i by the globally nonnegative measurable map prod max(y_i,0), which agrees on the support of the joint law, makes Tonelli apply immediately. The stated factorization is correct.

F1 is false for the periodic half-step because its second jump contributes; independently, the decomposition's h retains every other jump allowed by the theorem and therefore need not be continuous. The cited general piecewise-C1 Gibbs theorem supplies the correct local result.
Claims 2 and 5 are false when F has a left jump at b: the defining J_F includes it at x=b, but the displayed series and listed determining data omit it.

A one-line induction on the recursive finite-product definition shows that full n-fold measurable rectangles generate it. That immediate bridge supplies both measurability and the generating pi-system; the product-law proof is correct.

Indexing the at-most-countable discontinuity set by a subset A of N, exactly as the preceding split theorem does, removes repetitions and makes the discrete measure finite. This is an immediate local indexing correction; the measure-differentiation argument is sound.

The theorem assumes only Countable Choice but step 1.1 invokes the full Vitali theorem whose statement assumes Dependent Choice; the library explicitly records that Countable Choice does not supply DC.

Extending C_F constantly to the left of a and right of b gives a nondecreasing continuous, hence right-continuous, real-line function with a finite Stieltjes measure. This standard one-sentence extension makes every cited interval formula apply.

Applying rising sun to the negative of the reflected H, rather than to the reflection alone, gives exactly the displayed interval increment and bound. The missing minus sign is an immediately closable proof step.

Step 2.1's continuity inference is invalid when its witness lies to the left of d and does not prove the component endpoint conclusion. The primary-source proof requires a genuine maximal/supremal argument, so this is not a one-line sign or citation bridge.

The constant extension of F outside [a,b] is nondecreasing and right-continuous and has a finite Stieltjes measure of total mass F(b)-F(a). Stating this immediate extension makes the published real-line decomposition interfaces apply.

Defining g=liminf h_n first gives a total nonnegative measurable representative equal to F' wherever the derivative exists; Fatou applies directly to g. This immediate reordering removes the circular appeal to an a.e.-equality theorem.

The published outer-regularity theorem immediately supplies an open U with finite Lebesgue measure, and the published Lebesgue-measure interface identifies lambda. Adding those direct dependencies closes step 1.1 without changing the greedy proof or theorem.

rationale: The sole dependency statement gives only an unfiltered algebra isomorphism. Step 3.1 needs the nontrivial filtered PBW compatibility to prove the asserted generator degrees, so the cited interface does not license the conclusion.

Step 2.1 identifies the canonical tensor with the identity and explicitly invokes invariance of the Killing form; diagonal-adjoint invariance follows by the immediate bilinear calculation B([x,y],z)+B(y,[x,z])=0. A direct citation would improve the proof, but the omitted one-line bridge does not invalidate it.

The cited Harish-Chandra statement is only an unfiltered algebra isomorphism and does not export gr Z(U(g))=S(g)^g or invariant PBW lifts. Those facts are essential to the filtered-graded freeness argument and require a local derivation.

The word 'exactly' overlooks that the cited three-term sequence targets H^1(N,A), while restriction lands in H^1(N,A)^Q. This is a local codomain imprecision: the item separately assumes the full five-term sequence in A1, and the claimed kernel-image criterion follows directly from A1.

note: The construction is correct after the immediate indexing convention that the displayed enumeration is indexed by n>=1, exactly as the defining series is. Reindexing a countable enumeration by the positive integers closes the local proof gap without changing the claim or witness.

The equality c(v_n)-c(u_n)=2^-n follows immediately from claim 1 of the already cited direct dependency thm-cantor-function-properties together with the displayed ternary endpoints: c agrees with the binary digit map on the Cantor set. The sentence misattributes that one-line bridge to the definition alone, but the claim and secant argument are correct.

The displayed formula does not declare x or a domain for F, while continuous part and jump part are defined only for a function on a specified compact interval. The proof silently needs F:[0,1]->R, including the left jump at the endpoint 1; this is an ill-typed Example as written.

Continuity at 0 is an immediate endpoint version of step 2.1: choose N with small tail and then choose a right neighborhood below the positive minimum of q_1,...,q_N. The finite head is zero there and the tail is uniformly small, so J(x)->J(0)=0. The exact discontinuity set and zero endpoint defect are therefore correct, with only this one-line endpoint case omitted.

The non-absolute-continuity refutation depends on the exact stage-n Cantor intervals and their 2^-n image increments, but neither the Facts block nor a cited exact dependency statement supplies or derives those data. The BV witness is true, but its load-bearing refutation is unsupported as written.

Resetting only the single real point x_0 makes the constructed tilde f fail one-periodicity whenever its translates retain the old value, so the 2pi-periodic source theorem cannot be applied to g. The midpoint reset must be made on the entire congruence class x_0+Z, with the countable exceptional set shown null.

Claim 2 quantifies over any enumeration, which under the library's countability convention may repeat a discontinuity. The two nonnegative series then count repeated jump sizes repeatedly and need not equal J_F, so the theorem statement is false without a repetition-free indexing.

The converse needs only the immediate restriction to the family of all bounded nondegenerate closed intervals, which is visibly a fine cover of every E. With that one-word admissibility correction, condition 2 applies and the rest of the null-cover argument is unchanged.

An open subspace of [a,b) can have a component (a,d) when a is a boundary point not belonging to E. The stated dichotomy excludes this case, and the judge's continuous example has E=(0,1) on [0,2], so the component classification in the theorem is false as written.
The definition quantified over overline(F)-free graphs without defining the complement family or citing a complement-family interface.
The Given block called the four-vertex B_i singleton blocks, contradicting the construction and the width-four verification.
The conclusion falsely called 2^43 the first graph order above 2^42, although 2^42+1 is smaller and admissible.
L1 omitted the ell,w at least four hypotheses from property (*), so its universal dependency restatement was overstrong.
A fixed C^{n+1} shell bound does not dominate the independently varying finite derivative orders allowed in a basic strong neighborhood.
The library defines an (ell,w)-blockade for real ell by actual integral length t at least ell, equivalently t at least ceil(ell); the two formulations are exactly synonymous.

The item now constructs the inverse-image ring and module structures and the adjoint ring map; the generic tensor-sheaf definition applies to the ringed space (X,f^{-1}O_Y), so the displayed relative tensor is well typed.
The affine anti-equivalence was invoked without a local result establishing the principal open as an object in that theorem's narrow category; the repair verifies the inverse regular maps directly.
A rational function has many presentations, so regularity at the origin is equivalent to admitting a presentation with denominator nonzero at zero, not to every displayed denominator being nonzero.

The named relative Dirichlet density is the limiting ratio to the full prime sum; requiring an O(1) remainder is strictly stronger. The cited definition gives the ratio limit, equivalently an o(log(1/(s-1))) remainder.
The opened dependency proves exactly the clause-occurrence construction used here, and the example independently checks the displayed clique and satisfying assignment.
The item proves rational isotropy directly by the explicit nonzero vector (1,1,1,0); it does not infer isotropy from unverified local hypotheses.

The cited lemma did not license the asserted literal tiles or common word, and the toy machine omitted the required move direction. The repair specifies a clamped-left move and exhibits the exact initial tile sequence under the repaired construction.
The opened dependency explicitly gives the NAE conversion, variable triangles, and position-labelled clause triangles; the example also defines and colours its graph locally.

The proof changed to a cleanup machine but continued decoding transitions as those of the original machine, and its unnamed marker shift did not define the claimed domino system. The repair gives the exact standard tile families directly for the original clamped-left machine.
A zero of F at 1 makes log F singular, so the stated Landau contradiction is invalid. The repair instead uses log F(sigma)>=0, hence |F(sigma)|>=1, which directly excludes a zero at 1.

Multiplying by a rational square and permuting coordinates cannot normalize an arbitrary diagonal coefficient to 1. The repair uses similarity by a nonzero scalar and independent rational coordinate rescalings to choose squarefree representatives.

An isotropic first binary summand can give a local zero with t_v=0 even when q' is anisotropic. The repair explicitly rechooses the zero using universality of an isotropic binary form so that t_v is nonzero.
The opened definition of A_TM fixes it as a language of binary machine/input-pair codes, so the letter-by-letter relabelling into the two chosen symbols is licensed.

For the empty 3-CNF the construction references nonexistent first and last variable gadgets. The repair supplies the one-vertex path instance and its two-vertex cycle closure before assuming a nonempty clause list.

The proof handles every well-formed 3-CNF instance; extending the ambient-string map by sending malformed strings to any fixed non-3-colourable graph is an immediate decoder branch and does not affect the mathematical reduction.
The asserted residue list omits 2 modulo 8. Although 2 is also a nonsquare and the conclusion survives, the exhaustive computation as written is false and is corrected explicitly.

The opened dependency states and proves exactly the counterexample summarized in L1: the underlying hom-set bijection is present while the required enriched isomorphism E congruent to [X,E] is absent. The rejection inverted that dependency's conclusion.
Both outer composition subscripts in the associativity equation were reversed and hence ill-typed. The repair uses M_{A,B,D} after M_{B,C,D} and M_{A,C,D} after M_{A,B,C}.
Under the page's set-object V-category convention, the cited self-enrichment theorem requires V to have a set of objects. The definition now states that hypothesis before typing weights valued in V.

Universality alone does not supply the degree-zero identifications used in step 1.1. The repair cites the derived-delta theorem that gives L_0 naturally isomorphic to F and also states both abelian-category hypotheses.

The displayed resolution need not be the one in the supplied datum P. The repair computes with a datum Q using that resolution and invokes the exact comparison theorem to transfer the nonzero L_1 value back to P.

The title claimed extension from degree-zero data although the general n clauses require an existing partial morphism through the preceding degrees. It now names the actual one-step extension of a partial morphism.
The universal shuffle identity was undefined at p=0 or q=0. The proof now handles both zero-degree cases directly and invokes EZ_{p-1,q} and EZ_{p,q-1} only after assuming p,q>0.

L3 supplies only monicity and epicity, not the attributed defining equations. The repair constructs the projective and injective effacement ladders explicitly and derives both connecting-square equations from L1 and naturality.

The fixed-side horseshoe comparison theorem does not control changed end lifts. The repair separately invokes projective comparison uniqueness for the end lifts, then homotopy invariance on end homology, while retaining fixed-side uniqueness for middle maps.

The preceding theorem, already a direct frontmatter dependency, makes (L_n^P F) a homological delta functor under exactly these hypotheses. Invoking it before applying L3 is an immediate local proof step; the effacement argument and claim are correct.

The derived- and delta-functor dependencies require abelian source and target categories; additivity and exactness alone did not establish the target hypothesis. The statement now assumes both categories are abelian.

The repository's opened size convention defines categories with definable hom-collections, which may be proper classes, and reserves 'locally small' for set-valued homs. Mere monoidality therefore does suffice for the underlying category; local smallness is needed only to make its hom-collections sets.

The cited ordinary functor-category definition neither defines enriched hom-objects nor requires base limits. The repair says so explicitly and independently explains that a whole enriched functor category needs an enriched end for every functor pair.

A nonunit weight alone does not prove its representing object cannot be constructed conically. The repaired theorem makes the valid claim that conical weights are a proper subclass, and expressly notes that the Z/2 cotensor may be a conical equalizer of 2_C and 0_C.

F is not a functor on A^op and the cited theorem is an end formula, so step 2.1 did not yield co-Yoneda. The repair applies strong Yoneda on A^op to the correctly typed functor G_X(A)=[F(A),X] and derives the coend representation.

The injective-horseshoe interface alone did not state the short exact cochain sequence required for long exact cohomology. The repair derives that split sequence from the dual projective horseshoe and separately cites comparison-extension independence on cohomology.

The cited self-enrichment theorem requires V to have a set of objects under this page's convention; local smallness does not imply that. The statement and given data now include the exact size hypothesis.

The rejection itself observes that the proof retains the blockade's actual integral length. Steps 1.1–2.1 therefore meet the local real-threshold definition when changing the displayed lower length bound from r to floor(r); step 3.1 only weakens the required width. Source Lemma 5.5 states the same pure-or-x-sparse blockade conclusion.
